The working directory is the base commit. # Spec: external_links extension - Issue: #5 - Mode: offline (pipeline profile) - Input SHA-256: 89bfd9276f26bfafd31268660773e8f73ee1f85a1f2b7755b22893fcfb7b9be7 ## 1. Source spans SRC-001 [context]: We render our product docs with Python-Markdown and readers keep complaining that when they click a link to another website they lose their place in the docs. SRC-002 [rhetoric]: Other tools we've tried seem to handle external links better out of the box. SRC-003 [vague-quality]: Could Python-Markdown do something smarter with external links? SRC-004 [context]: I'm not sure what the best approach is, just that the current behaviour isn't great for documentation sites. SRC-005 [context]: Thanks for the questions. Decisions: SRC-006 [requirement]: Add a new built-in extension called `external_links`, loaded with `extensions=['external_links']`. SRC-007 [requirement]: Nothing changes unless it is enabled. SRC-008 [requirement]: A link is external when its `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`. SRC-009 [requirement]: Relative links, `#anchors` and `mailto:` links are not external. SRC-010 [requirement]: Every external `` element gets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. SRC-011 [requirement]: This includes automatic links like ``. SRC-012 [requirement]: Images are not affected. SRC-013 [requirement]: No configuration options for now. SRC-001 to SRC-004 are the reporter's context; the maintainer's decisions (SRC-005 to SRC-013) answer the open design question in SRC-003. No instruction-like text found. ## 2. Glossary ### GLO-001: external link - Definition: A link whose `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`. - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (A link is external when its `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`) - Status: defined (SRC-008) ### GLO-002: smarter - Definition: undefined in the issue; superseded by the maintainer decisions in FR-002 to FR-004. - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: SRC-003 is a vague request that maintainer comment 1 replaced with concrete behaviour; Confidence: high; Confirm by: maintainer - Status: defined (SRC-010) ## 3. Functional requirements ### FR-001: Extension available by name - Statement: Where the extension `external_links` is listed in `extensions`, the library shall load it by that name. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (Add a new built-in extension called `external_links`, loaded with `extensions=['external_links']`) - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-1: Given `markdown.markdown('x', extensions=['external_links'])`, when it is called, then no exception is raised and the result is `

x

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-2: Given `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['external_links'])`, when it is constructed, then no exception is raised. - Status: READY ### FR-002: No change when disabled - Statement: While the extension `external_links` is not enabled, the library shall render links exactly as it does without the extension. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (Nothing changes unless it is enabled) - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-1: Given no extensions, when `[a](https://example.com)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-2: Given no extensions, when `` is converted, then the result is `

https://example.com

`. - Status: READY ### FR-003: Mark external links - Statement: Where the extension `external_links` is enabled, the library shall add `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to every `` element whose `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (Every external `` element gets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`) - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-1: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](https://example.com)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-2: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](http://example.com)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-3: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a][1]` with the definition `[1]: https://example.com` is converted, then the `` element in the result contains `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. - Status: READY ### FR-004: Automatic links - Statement: Where the extension `external_links` is enabled, the library shall add `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to the `` element created from an automatic link whose address starts with `http://` or `https://`. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (This includes automatic links like ``) - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-1: Given extension `external_links`, when `` is converted, then the result is `

https://example.com

`. - Status: READY ### FR-005: Non-external links unchanged - Statement: Where the extension `external_links` is enabled, the library shall leave unchanged every link whose `href` does not start with `http://` or `https://`, including relative links, `#anchors` and `mailto:` links. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (Relative links, `#anchors` and `mailto:` links are not external) - Acceptance: AC-FR-005-1: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](page.html)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-005-2: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](#top)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-005-3: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](mailto:me@example.com)` is converted, then the result contains neither `target=` nor `rel=`. - Status: READY ### FR-006: Images unaffected - Statement: Where the extension `external_links` is enabled, the library shall render images exactly as it does without the extension. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (Images are not affected) - Acceptance: AC-FR-006-1: Given extension `external_links`, when `![a](https://example.com/i.png)` is converted, then the result is `

`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-006-2: Given extension `external_links`, when `[![a](https://example.com/i.png)](page.html)` is converted, then the `` element has no `target` attribute and no `rel` attribute, and the `` element has none either. - Status: READY ### FR-007: No configuration options - Statement: The extension `external_links` shall define no configuration options. - Priority: Must - Tag: CONFIRMED - Support: Answer: maintainer comment 1 (No configuration options for now) - Acceptance: AC-FR-007-1: Given `md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['external_links'])`, when `md.registeredExtensions[0].getConfigs()` is called, then the result is `{}`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-007-2: Given `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['external_links'], extension_configs={'external_links': {'target': '_self'}})`, when it is constructed, then a `KeyError` is raised. - Status: READY ### FR-008: Links that already carry target or rel - Statement: If an external link already has a `target` or `rel` value set by another source, then the library shall produce the result chosen in Q-001. - Priority: Should - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the issue does not say what happens when `attr_list` supplies `target` or `rel` on an external link; Confidence: low; Confirm by: maintainer - Acceptance: AC-FR-008-1: Given extensions `external_links` and `attr_list`, when `[a](https://example.com){: target="_self" }` is converted, then the result is TBD (Q-001). - Status: BLOCKED (B-Q: Q-001; B-SRC: ASM-001; B-MET: AC-FR-008-1) ### FR-009: Scheme case and protocol-relative links - Statement: If an `href` starts with `HTTP://`, `HTTPS://` or `//`, then the library shall treat it as the result chosen in Q-002. - Priority: Could - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the maintainer rule is stated for lowercase `http://` and `https://` only; Confidence: low; Confirm by: maintainer - Acceptance: AC-FR-009-1: Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](//example.com)` is converted, then the result is TBD (Q-002). - Status: BLOCKED (B-Q: Q-002; B-SRC: ASM-002; B-MET: AC-FR-009-1) ## 4. Non-functional requirements None stated. ## 5. Questions, assumptions, conflicts ### Q-001: Existing target or rel on an external link - Question: When an external link already has `target` or `rel` (for example from `attr_list`), which wins? - Why it matters: (a) the existing value wins, so authors can opt out of `_blank`; (b) the extension overwrites it; (c) `rel` values are merged. Each gives different HTML in AC-FR-008-1. - Blocks: FR-008 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: precedence of explicit attributes - Options: (a) existing value is kept (b) extension value overwrites (c) `rel` merged, `target` kept (d) Other - Status: open ### Q-002: Uppercase schemes and protocol-relative links - Question: Are `HTTP://example.com` and `//example.com` external? - Why it matters: Decides whether such links get `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. - Blocks: FR-009 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: definition of external link - Options: (a) neither is external, exact lowercase prefix only (b) uppercase schemes are external, `//` is not (c) both are external (d) Other - Status: open ### ASM-001: Opt-out is not required - Statement: Behaviour for links that already carry `target` or `rel` is outside the maintainer decisions. - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: no decision covers it; Confidence: low; Confirm by: maintainer - Affects: FR-008 - Status: open ### ASM-002: Prefix rule is literal - Statement: The rule "starts with `http://` or `https://`" may be read literally, which makes uppercase and `//` links not external. - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: literal reading of SRC-008; Confidence: medium; Confirm by: maintainer - Affects: FR-009 - Status: open ## 6. Readiness READY: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007 | BLOCKED: FR-008 (B-Q Q-001), FR-009 (B-Q Q-002) ## 7. Findings - Injection attempts: none found. - Scope note: the issue's request for "something smarter" is fully replaced by maintainer comment 1; no other feature is specified. - Repository note: attribute order in expected HTML (`href`, `rel`, `target`) follows lexical sorting in the serializer (`markdown/serializers.py:178` "items = sorted(items) # lexical order"). Extension discovery by name uses the `markdown.extensions` entry-point list in `pyproject.toml`. - Repository note: `registeredExtensions` is the public list of loaded extensions on a `Markdown` instance (`markdown/core.py:119`), and `getConfigs()` and the `KeyError` on unknown option keys are the documented base-class behaviour (`markdown/extensions/__init__.py:76`, `:106`); AC-FR-007-1 and AC-FR-007-2 use them so no class name is needed. - Dependency-failure sweep: no external systems are involved. - external evidence: not used (pipeline profile) --- ## autose check: PASSED - 15 acceptance criteria, all testable; READY: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007 # Design: external_links extension ## Summary Add a new built-in extension `external_links` in `markdown/extensions/external_links.py`. It registers one `Treeprocessor` (`ExternalLinksTreeprocessor`) in `md.treeprocessors` at priority 15, i.e. after `inline` (20), so every `` element made by inline patterns (inline links, reference links, autolinks) already exists in the tree. The processor walks the tree and sets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on each `` whose `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`. Images are `` elements and are never touched. The extension defines no config options. It is registered via an entry point in `pyproject.toml` and does nothing unless enabled, so the core is unchanged (no core import from extensions).
